verses.zh: 「你若留意听从耶和华―你　神的话，谨守遵行他的一切诫命，就是我今日所吩咐你的，他必使你超乎天下万民之上。
verses.en: “If you indeed[NOTE:1] obey the Lord your God and are careful to observe all his commandments I am giving[NOTE:2] you today, the Lord your God will elevate you above all the nations of the earth.
notes: The Hebrew text uses the infinitive absolute for emphasis, which the translation indicates with “indeed.”
Heb “commanding”; NAB “which I enjoin on you today” (likewise in v. 15).
verses.commentary:
28:1,2,9,13 "if you will" This clearly shows the conditional nature of the Mosaic Law and for that matter, most OT covenants.
This conditional aspect is also seen in the NT (cf. Mark 1:15; Acts 20:21 and Eph. 2:8-9 and 10). The
"if you will . . .I will" nature of the covenant shows the needed response expected on the believer's part. The tragedy is that fallen
humanity cannot and will not conform or perform, therefore, the OT demands the need for a NT (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-32;
Rom. 3:10-18,23; Gal. 3:15-29).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

28:1,2,13 "diligently obey. . .being careful to do all His commandments" The first VERBAL "diligently
obey" is an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and a Qal IMPERFECT of the same root (BDB 1033,
KB 1570), which was a grammatical way of showing emphasis. This is followed by two Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS:

- "being careful" ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581

- "to do" ‒ BDB 793, KB 889

It must be stated that believers' ongoing covenant relationship with God is affected by their obedience.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "commandments" See SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

▣ "which I command you today" This VERB (BDB 845, KB 1010, Piel PARTICIPLE)
is repeated throughout this chapter (cf. Deut. 28:1,8,13,15,45). YHWH is sovereign. He always sets the limits and content of the
covenant and initiates the encounter with humans (i.e. John 6:44,65). However, He also demands an initial and continuing human response
(i.e. repentance, faith, obedience, service, worship, perseverance)!

28:1 "God will set you high above all the nations of the earth" The purpose of the elevation of Israel is the elevation
of YHWH (cf. Deut. 26:19; 28:13)! God wants to draw the world to Himself through Israel (cf. Gen. 12:3; 22:18;Exod. 19:5-6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 你若听从耶和华―你　神的话，这以下的福必追随你，临到你身上：
verses.en: All these blessings will come to you in abundance[NOTE:1] if you obey the Lord your God:
notes: Heb “come upon you and overtake you” (so NASB, NRSV); NIV11 “come on you and accompany you.”
verses.commentary:
28:2 "blessings" The term (BDB 139) is related to the root "to kneel" (BDB 138). YHWH offers Israel the choice
(cf. Deut. 11:26-31; 30:1,19). This conformity to YHWH's covenant requirements determines their destiny!

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING (OT)

▣ "will come upon you" This idiomatic phrase (BDB 97, KB 112, Qal PERFECT
with waw) is used here for blessing, but in Deut. 28:15 for the curses.

▣ "overtake" The VERB (BDB 673, KB 727, Hiphil PERFECT
with waw) is used of:

- blessing, pursuing, and overtaking Israel because of her obedience, Deut. 28:2

- cursing, pursuing, and overtaking Israel because of her disobedience, Deut. 28:15,45

▣ "obey" In Deut. 28:1 this term (BDB 1033, KB 1570) was an intensified Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
and a Qal IMPERFECT. Here it is a Qal IMPERFECT (cf. Deut. 28:15,49; 30:10,12,13,17;
31:12) and in Deut. 28:45, 62 a Qal PERFECT (cf. Deut. 30:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

verses.zh: 你在城里必蒙福，在田间也必蒙福。
verses.en: You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the field.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “in the country” (so NAB, NIV, NLT). This expression also occurs in v. 15.
verses.commentary:
28:3 "Blessed shall you be in the city. . .in the country" This is imagery of expressing
a nation wide blessing (cf. Deut. 28:4-6, 8).

verses.zh: 你身所生的，地所产的，牲畜所下的，以及牛犊、羊羔，都必蒙福。
verses.en: Your children[NOTE:1] will be blessed, as well as the produce of your soil, the offspring of your livestock, the calves of your herds, and the lambs of your flocks.
notes: Heb “the fruit of your womb” (so NAB, NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 你的筐子和你的抟面盆都必蒙福。
verses.en: Your basket and your mixing bowl will be blessed.
verses.commentary:
28:5 "Blessed. . .basket" This basket was used to carry fruit or grain (cf. Deut. 26:2). This speaks of prosperity in agriculture.

▣ "Blessed. . .kneading bowl" This was a bowl used to prepare family meals (i.e. daily bread). This was a way
of saying, "there will always be food on the table." The opposite is stated in Deut. 28:17.

verses.zh: 你出也蒙福，入也蒙福。
verses.en: You will be blessed when you come in and blessed when you go out.[NOTE:1]
notes: Come in…go out. To “come in” and “go out” is a figure of speech (merism) indicating all of life and its activities.
verses.commentary:
28:6 "Blessed. . .when you come in. . .when you go out" This is a Hebraic idiom (cf. Deut. 31:2; Ps. 121:8; Isa. 37:28) for a
blessed life in all areas (cf. contrast in Deut. 28:19).

verses.zh: 「仇敌起来攻击你，耶和华必使他们在你面前被你杀败；他们从一条路来攻击你，必从七条路逃跑。
verses.en: The Lord will cause your enemies who attack[NOTE:1] you to be struck down before you; they will attack you from one direction[NOTE:2] but flee from you in seven different directions.
notes: Heb “who rise up against” (so NIV).
Heb “way” (also later in this verse and in v. 25).
verses.commentary:
28:7 "Lord" This is the Hebrew word "Lord" (Adon).

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (Adon and Kurios)

▣ "enemies" This PARTICIPLE (BDB 33, KB 38 Qal PARTICIPLE) is used
eight times in this chapter (cf. Deut. 28:7,25,31,48,53,55,57,68). It refers to the active hostility of a person or group against
a person or group. YHWH promised to be an enemy to Israel's enemies (cf. Exod. 23:22), but because of covenant disobedience
He is now an enemy to Israel!

If Israel is obedient, YHWH will fight her enemies (i.e. Divine Warrior, "holy war" terminology, cf. Deut. 30:7; 33:27-29).

▣ "will flee before you seven ways" This idiom refers to the fearful, unorganized retreat of Israel's enemies
(cf. Deut. 28:20, 25).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #4

verses.zh: 在你仓房里，并你手所办的一切事上，耶和华所命的福必临到你。耶和华―你　神也要在所给你的地上赐福与你。
verses.en: The Lord will decree blessing for you with respect to your barns and in everything you do—yes, he will bless you in the land he[NOTE:1] is giving you.
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” Because English would not typically reintroduce the proper name following a relative pronoun (“he will bless…the Lord your God is giving”), the pronoun (“he”) has been employed here in the translation.
verses.commentary:
28:8 "blessing upon. . .barns" This refers to grain storehouses (cf. Prov. 3:10). Later Judaism says this refers to
YHWH blessing one in secret.

▣ "in the land which the Lord your God gives you" This goes back to the promise
to Abraham in Gen. 12:1-3. The land was YHWH's special promise fulfilled in the exodus/conquest.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

verses.zh: 你若谨守耶和华―你　神的诫命，遵行他的道，他必照着向你所起的誓立你作为自己的圣民。
verses.en: The Lord will designate you as his holy people just as he promised you, if you keep his commandments[NOTE:1] and obey him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the commandments of the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in the previous verse.
Heb “and walk in his ways” (so NAB, NASB, NIV84, NRSV, NLT).
verses.commentary:
28:9 "the Lord will establish you" This VERB (BDB 877, KB 1086, Hiphil
IMPERFECT) basically means "to raise up." It is used in several different senses in Deuteronomy in the Hiphil.

- confirm a covenant, cf. Deut. 8:18

- being on the scene, cf. Deut. 18:15,18

- raise up fallen livestock, cf. Deut. 22:4

- to set up memorial stones, cf. Deut. 27:3)

Here it is used as imagery in the sense of "establish," as in Deut. 25:7 and 29:13.

▣ "Lord" See SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "a holy people" The word "holy" means "set apart for God's service" (BDB 871 and 872). Israel was meant to
be a kingdom of priests to bring all the nations to YHWH (i.e. Ezod. 19:5-6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "walk" This is a biblical imagery for lifestyle faith and obedience (cf. Deut. 5:33; 8:6; 10:12; 11:22; 19:9; 26:17; 30:16).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

verses.zh: 天下万民见你归在耶和华的名下，就要惧怕你。
verses.en: Then all the peoples of the earth will see that you belong to the Lord,[NOTE:1] and they will respect you.
notes: Heb “the name of the Lord is called over you.” The Hebrew idiom indicates ownership; see 2 Sam 12:28; Isa 4:1, as well as BDB 896 s.v. קָרָא Niph. 2.d.(4).
verses.commentary:
28:10 "So all the peoples of the earth will see that you are called by the name of the Lord" The
phrase "called by the name of the Lord" (BDB 894, KB 1128, Niphal PERFECT)
denotes YHWH's ownership of Israel (cf. 2 Sam. 6:2; Isa. 43:7; Jer. 7:10-12; 14:9; 15:16; 32:34; Dan. 9:18,19; Amos 9:12).

YHWH wanted Israel to be a revelatory channel for all the world to come to know Him. He wanted to bless
Israel to gain the attention of the nations and thereby to attract the nations unto Himself (cf. Deut. 28:25, 37).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

▣ "afraid of you" The blessings of YHWH, both in domestic and military areas, will cause fear/reverence
(BDB 431, KB 432, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 7:19; 17:13) on the part of superstitious
pagans of the surrounding nations.

Israel was not to fear (BDB 431, KB 432) because YHWH was with them, for them, and fought on their behalf
(e.g. Deut. 1:21,29; 3:2,22; 7:18; 20:1,3; 31:6,8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

verses.zh: 你在耶和华向你列祖起誓应许赐你的地上，他必使你身所生的，牲畜所下的，地所产的，都绰绰有余。
verses.en: The Lord will greatly multiply your children,[NOTE:1] the offspring of your livestock, and the produce of your soil in the land that he[NOTE:2] promised your ancestors[NOTE:3] he would give you.
notes: Heb “the fruit of your womb” (so NAB, NIV, NRSV); CEV “will give you a lot of children.”
Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 28:8.
Heb “fathers” (also in vv. 36, 64).
verses.commentary: 28:11 This is a summary verse of YHWH's blessing to an obedient covenant people (e.g. Deut. 11:14).

verses.zh: 耶和华必为你开天上的府库，按时降雨在你的地上。在你手里所办的一切事上赐福与你。你必借给许多国民，却不致向他们借贷。
verses.en: The Lord will open for you his good treasure house, the heavens, to give you rain for the land in its season and to bless all you do;[NOTE:1] you will lend to many nations but you will not borrow from any.
notes: Heb “all the work of your hands.”
verses.commentary:
28:12 "His good storehouse" This (BDB 373 II and 69) was a symbol of heaven and rain (cf. Deut. 28:23-24; Ps. 85:12;
Mal. 3:10). It is possibly a sarcastic reference to Ba'al worship. Ba'al was the Canaanite god of prosperity
(i.e. rain, cf. 1 Kings 17-18). Yet, it was YHWH who provided all blessings to His people (cf. Deut. 28:47; 11:14; Lev. 26:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

▣ "to give rain to your land in its season" This VERB (BDB 678, KB 733) is used regularly
in this chapter for YHWH's covenant gifts of blessing (cf. Deut. 28:1,7,8,11,12,13).

Not only will YHWH open the windows of heaven and send rain, but He will do it at the appropriate time
(i.e. early and later rains, the time of planting and the time of maturing crops).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

▣ "you shall lend to many nations but you shall not borrow" This was another sign of God's blessing that
they had surplus to loan (cf. Deut. 23:20)! The results of disobedience are sharply contrasted in Deut. 28:44!

verses.zh: 你若听从耶和华―你　神的诫命，就是我今日所吩咐你的，谨守遵行，不偏左右，也不随从事奉别神，耶和华就必使你作首不作尾，但居上不居下。」
verses.en: The Lord will make you the head and not the tail, and you will always end up at the top and not at the bottom, if you obey his[NOTE:1] commandments that I am urging[NOTE:2] you today to be careful to do.
notes: Heb “the Lord your God’s.” See note on “he” in 28:8.
Heb “commanding” (so NRSV); NASB “which I charge you today.”
verses.commentary:
28:13 This verse has two idioms of prosperity and power:

- the head and not the tail

- you only shall be above, not be underneath

But note the conditional element. The same idiom was used in Deut. 28:1, "being careful to do"
(two INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS). The reversal caused by disobedience is seen in Deut. 28:44.

verses.zh: a
verses.en: But you must not turn away from all the commandments I am giving[NOTE:1] you today, to either the right or left, nor pursue other gods and worship[NOTE:2] them.
notes: Heb “from all the words which I am commanding.”
Heb “in order to serve.”
verses.commentary:
28:14 "do not turn aside. . .to the right or to the left" It is used literally in Num. 20:17; 22:26; Deut. 2:27, but usually
it is a Hebrew idiom for "any deviation from the standard or clearly marked path is sin" (cf. Deut. 5:32; 17:11,20; Josh. 1:7; 23:6;
2 Kgs. 22:2). Notice here, idolatry is specifically referenced (cf. Deut. 5:7-9; 27:15; Exod. 20:23; 34:17).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

verses.zh: 「你若不听从耶和华―你　神的话，不谨守遵行他的一切诫命律例，就是我今日所吩咐你的，这以下的咒诅都必追随你，临到你身上：
verses.en: “But if you ignore[NOTE:1] the Lord your God and are not careful to keep all his commandments and statutes I am giving you today, then all these curses will come upon you in full force:[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “do not hear the voice of.”
Heb “and overtake you” (so NIV, NRSV); NAB, NLT “and overwhelm you.”
verses.commentary:
28:15-37 This section of cursings does not demand a literal interpretation. Rather, they were to build up
an impression of disaster. These kinds of blights will follow if disobedience occurs. It was a way of building up a
mindset on what will happen if Israel violates YHWH's law.

28:15 "to observe to do" This is the exact terminology and grammatical form found in Deut. 28:1,13; 32:46. Similar
forms of the same terms are found in Deut. 28:58 and 29:8. Obedience is crucial. Obedience is not the foundation of the
covenant, but its natural outflow! The covenant is established in the love and sovereignty of YHWH, but its continuance
and fruitfulness is maintained by obedience.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "His commandments and His statutes" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

▣ "curses" This is a NOUN form from the root "to be small" (BDB 886-887,
cf. Deut. 27:15-26, 28:15-68). These curses were meant to cause Israel to return to YHWH.

▣ "overtake" This is a personification of curses. See note at Deut. 28:2.

verses.zh: 你在城里必受咒诅，在田间也必受咒诅。
verses.en: You will be cursed in the city and cursed in the field.
verses.commentary: 28:16-19 These verses parallel completely. Verses 3-6 are the blessings; Deut. 28:16-19 are the cursings.

verses.zh: 你的筐子和你的抟面盆都必受咒诅。
verses.en: Your basket and your mixing bowl will be cursed.

verses.zh: 你身所生的，地所产的，以及牛犊、羊羔，都必受咒诅。
verses.en: Your children[NOTE:1] will be cursed, as well as the produce of your soil, the calves of your herds, and the lambs of your flocks.
notes: Heb “the fruit of your womb” (so NAB, NIV, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
28:18

NASB, NJB
"offspring of your body"

NKJV, Peshitta
"fruit of your body"

NRSV
"fruit of your womb"

TEV
"children"

LXX
"the progeny of your belly"

JPSOA
"the issue of your womb"

The literal phrase is, "the fruit of your womb." Many healthy, happy children were one of the
blessings (cf. Deut. 28:4,11), but disobedience brought covenant promise reversal!

verses.zh: 你出也受咒诅，入也受咒诅。
verses.en: You will be cursed when you come in and cursed when you go out.[NOTE:1]
notes: See note on the similar expression in v. 6.

verses.zh: 耶和华因你行恶离弃他，必在你手里所办的一切事上，使咒诅、扰乱、责罚临到你，直到你被毁灭，速速地灭亡。
verses.en: “The Lord will send on you a curse, confusing you and opposing you[NOTE:1] in everything you undertake[NOTE:2] until you are destroyed and quickly perish because of the evil of your deeds, in that you have forsaken me.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the curse, the confusion, and the rebuke” (NASB and NIV similar); NRSV “disaster, panic, and frustration.”
Heb “in all the stretching out of your hand.”

Heb “the evil of your doings wherein you have forsaken me”; CEV “all because you rejected the Lord.”tc For the MT first person common singular suffix (“me”), the LXX reads either “Lord” (Lucian) or third person masculine singular suffix (“him”; various codices). The MT’s more difficult reading probably represents the original text.
verses.commentary:
28:20 "confusion" This is a word (BDB 223) that is used of defeat in battle (cf. Deut. 7:23). It is opposite of
Deut. 28:7 and 25. The confusion will be upon Israel if she disobeys God's word.

▣

NASB, NKJV, REB, Peshitta
"rebuke"

NRSV, JPSOA
"frustration"

TEV
"trouble"

LXX
"exhaustion"

KB 546
"threat"

This root, מגערת (BDB 172, KB 546) is found only here. It is similar
to the root for "rebuke," גערה, found mostly in Job and Psalms. It relates to YHWH's destruction
of disobedient Israel in battle. For these rare words, modern interpreters look at

- context

- related Hebrew roots

- cognate roots

- if poetry, parallelism

▣ "until you are destroyed and until you perish quickly" Notice the parallelism:

- "destroyed" ‒ BDB 1029, KB 1552, Niphal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Deut. 4:26; 6:15

- "perish" ‒ BDB 1, KB 2, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Lev. 26:38; Deut. 4:26;
8:19-20; 11:17; 30:18-20; Josh. 23:13,16 plus the ADVERB "quickly" (BDB 555 II)

▣ "on account of the evil of your deeds, because you have forsaken Me" Notice that deviation from
the commandments is seen as forsaking YHWH!

verses.zh: 耶和华必使瘟疫贴在你身上，直到他将你从所进去得为业的地上灭绝。
verses.en: The Lord will plague you with deadly diseases[NOTE:1] until he has completely removed you from the land you are about to possess.
notes: Heb “will cause pestilence to cling to you.”
verses.commentary:
28:21 "pestilence" This (BDB 184) refers to a plague (cf. Lev. 26:25; Num. 14:12) like YHWH sent on Egypt (cf. Exod. 5:3; 9:15).

▣ "cling" The VERB (BDB 179, KB 209, Hiphil) is JUSSIVE in form. YHWH's
judgment will stick close to them until it has finished its task (i.e. "consumed you," BDB 477, KB 476, Piel
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT).

The same term is used for what Israel should do to YHWH (i.e. cling to Him, cf. Deut. 10:20; 11:22; 30:20). What irony!

verses.zh: 耶和华要用痨病、热病、火症、疟疾、刀剑、旱风（或译：干旱）、霉烂攻击你。这都要追赶你，直到你灭亡。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] will afflict you with weakness,[NOTE:2] fever, inflammation, infection,[NOTE:3] sword,[NOTE:4] blight, and mildew; these will attack you until you perish.
notes: Heb “The Lord.” See note on “he” in 28:8.
Or perhaps “consumption” (so KJV, NASB, NRSV). The term is from a verbal root that indicates a weakening of one’s physical strength (cf. NAB “wasting”; NIV, NLT “wasting disease”).
Heb “hot fever”; NIV “scorching heat.”
Or “drought” (so NIV, NRSV, NLT).
verses.commentary:
28:22 Note the list of things YHWH will send against a disobedient Israel:

- consumption (BDB 1006, cf. Lev. 26:16), a disease of the lungs

- fever (BDB 869, cf. Lev. 26:16)

- inflamation (BDB 196)

- fiery heat (BDB 359, #2,3, and 4 all involve heat; this one seems to imply drought conditions, cf. NRSV)

- sword (BDB 352; see note below)

- blight (BDB 995, smut on crops, cf. 1 Kgs. 8:37; 2 Chr. 6:28; Amos 4:9)

- mildew (BDB 439, cf. 1 Kgs. 8:37; 2 Chr. 6:28; Amos 4:9; Hag. 2:17; the word means "green," therefore, a "green mildew")

Both humans and agriculture will suffer and die! Notice the symbolic number of afflictions (i.e. seven; there
are also seven blessings listed in this chapter).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #4

▣

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta
"sword"

NRSV, NJB, TEV, JPSOA, REB
"drought"

LXX
"murder"

The Hebrew root, חרב, has several meanings

- drought ‒ BDB 351 I

- desolation ‒ BDB 351 II

- sword ‒ BDB 352

Number 3 has the Masoretic vowel marks, but UBS Text Project, p. 295, gives "drought" a "C" rating (considerable
doubt). The list itself suggests an agricultural judgment.

Remember, the Masoretic notes are not inspired. They were added to a Hebrew consonantal text much later
in Israel's history (i.e. started in A.D. 70 and finished in A.D. 900). They codify Israel's ancient traditions.

verses.zh: 你头上的天要变为铜，脚下的地要变为铁。
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] sky[NOTE:2] above your heads will be bronze and the earth beneath you iron.
notes: The MT reads “Your.” The LXX reads “Heaven will be to you.”
Or “heavens” (also in the following verse). The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heaven(s)” or “sky” depending on the context.
verses.commentary:
28:23 "iron" Iron is often imagery for difficulties:

- the land will not produce, because of no rain it turns as hard as metal, Deut. 28:23, cf. Lev. 26:19

- the yoke of iron is placed on Israel's neck, Deut. 28:48

- Egypt as an iron furnace of affliction, cf. Deut. 4:20

SPECIAL TOPIC: MASORETIC TEXT

verses.zh: 耶和华要使那降在你地上的雨变为尘沙，从天临在你身上，直到你灭亡。
verses.en: The Lord will make the rain of your land powder and dust; it will come down on you from the sky until you are destroyed.

verses.zh: 「耶和华必使你败在仇敌面前，你从一条路去攻击他们，必从七条路逃跑。你必在天下万国中抛来抛去。
verses.en: “The Lord will allow you to be struck down before your enemies; you will attack them from one direction but flee from them in seven directions and will become an object of terror[NOTE:1] to all the kingdoms of the earth.
notes: The meaningless MT reading זַעֲוָה (zaʿavah) is clearly a transposition of the more commonly attested Hebrew noun זְוָעָה (zevaʿah, “terror”).
verses.commentary:
28:25 "you will go out one way against them, but you will flee seven ways before them" This is imagery describing
Israel's military planning as being totally useless. Seven is a numerical symbol for "perfection." Israel will be in total retreat. The
promises of "holy war" have been reversed!

▣ "you will be an example of terror to all the kingdoms of the earth" Israel will be used by YHWH to reveal
Himself to the world; either positively (i.e. the blessings) or negatively (i.e. the curses, cf. Deut. 28:37; 2 Chr. 29:8; Jer. 15:4). YHWH
wanted to use Israel to reach all mankind. This is a reversal of His purposes!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 你的尸首必给空中的飞鸟和地上的走兽作食物，并无人哄赶。
verses.en: Your carcasses will be food for every bird of the sky and wild animal of the earth, and there will be no one to chase them off.
verses.commentary:
28:26 "Your carcasses shall be food" For Israel it was a great tragedy to be unburied and thus able to be picked apart
by animals (cf. 1 Sam. 17:44-46). Because of the mentioning of "birds," many see this as an eschatological reference
(cf. Isa. 18:14; Jer. 7:33; 16:4; 19:7; 34:20; Ezek. 29:5; 32:4; 39:4).

verses.zh: 耶和华必用埃及人的疮并痔疮、牛皮癣与疥攻击你，使你不能医治。
verses.en: The Lord will afflict you with the boils of Egypt and with tumors, eczema, and scabies, all of which cannot be healed.
verses.commentary:
28:27 "with the boils of Egypt" Notice the list of plagues and problems (plagues of Egypt now on Israel are a reversal of covenant
blessings) YHWH will visit on Israel if they do not obey His covenant. To whom much is given, much is required (e.g. Luke 12:48).

verses.zh: 耶和华必用癫狂、眼瞎、心惊攻击你。
verses.en: The Lord will also subject you to madness, blindness, and confusion of mind.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “heart” (so KJV, NASB).

verses.zh: 你必在午间摸索，好像瞎子在暗中摸索一样。你所行的必不亨通，时常遭遇欺压、抢夺，无人搭救。
verses.en: You will feel your way along at noon like the blind person does in darkness and you will not succeed in anything you do;[NOTE:1] you will be constantly oppressed and continually robbed, with no one to save you.
notes: Heb “you will not cause your ways to prosper.”

verses.zh: 你聘定了妻，别人必与她同房；你建造房屋，不得住在其内；你栽种葡萄园，也不得用其中的果子。
verses.en: You will be engaged to a woman, and another man will rape[NOTE:1] her. You will build a house but not live in it. You will plant a vineyard but not even begin to use it.
notes: For MT reading שָׁגַל (shagal, “ravish; violate”), the Syriac, Targum, and Vulgate presume the less violent שָׁכַב (shakhav, “lie with”). The unexpected counterpart to betrothal here favors the originality of the MT.

verses.zh: 你的牛在你眼前宰了，你必不得吃它的肉；你的驴在你眼前被抢夺，不得归还；你的羊归了仇敌，无人搭救。
verses.en: Your ox will be slaughtered before your very eyes, but you will not eat of it. Your donkey will be stolen from you as you watch and will not be returned to you. Your flock of sheep will be given to your enemies, and there will be no one to save you.

verses.zh: 你的儿女必归与别国的民；你的眼目终日切望，甚至失明，你手中无力拯救。
verses.en: Your sons and daughters will be given to another people while you look on in vain all day, and you will be powerless to do anything about it.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and there will be no power in your hand”; NCV “there will be nothing you can do.”
verses.commentary:
28:32 Notice the plight of these Israeli parents:

- children given to other people (BDB 678, KB 733, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE)

- they see it happening (BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE)

- their eyes fail with longing all the day (the term, BDB 479, is found only here in the OT)

- they have no power to stop it (BDB 34 II, CONSTRUCT BDB 43)

I can only imagine the horror and pain!

verses.zh: 你的土产和你劳碌得来的，必被你所不认识的国民吃尽。你时常被欺负，受压制，
verses.en: As for the produce of your land and all your labor, a people you do not know will consume it, and you will be nothing but oppressed and crushed for the rest of your lives.
verses.commentary:
28:33 "oppressed" This term was used regularly of the wealthy taking advantage of the poor and socially
ostracized, but here it is used of YHWH breaking His disobedient people.

verses.zh: 甚至你因眼中所看见的，必致疯狂。
verses.en: You will go insane from seeing all this.

verses.zh: 耶和华必攻击你，使你膝上腿上，从脚掌到头顶，长毒疮无法医治。
verses.en: The Lord will afflict you in your knees and on your legs with painful, incurable boils—from the soles of your feet to the top of your head.
verses.commentary:
28:35 "from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head" This is imagery for widespread sickness of which
one cannot be healed (cf. Job 2:7; in Isa. 1:5-6 it is a symbol of sin).

verses.zh: 「耶和华必将你和你所立的王领到你和你列祖素不认识的国去；在那里你必事奉木头石头的神。
verses.en: The Lord will force you and your king[NOTE:1] whom you will appoint over you to go away to a people whom you and your ancestors have not known, and you will serve other gods of wood and stone there.
notes: The LXX reads the plural “kings.”
verses.commentary:
28:36 "your king" Moses recognized that there would be a king someday (cf. Deut. 17:14-20). The Israelites
were a tribal society. There was no king until Saul (cf. 1 Samuel 8).

verses.zh: 你在耶和华领你到的各国中，要令人惊骇、笑谈、讥诮。
verses.en: You will become an occasion of horror, a proverb, and an object of ridicule to all the peoples to whom the Lord will drive you.

verses.zh: 你带到田间的种子虽多，收进来的却少，因为被蝗虫吃了。
verses.en: “You will take much seed to the field but gather little harvest, because locusts will consume it.
verses.commentary:
28:38-42 Again notice the list of Israel's attempts at prosperity, which will be thwarted
by YHWH:

Their Actions
Results

1.
much seed, Deut. 28:38
locusts destroy

2.
plant vineyards, Deut. 28:39
worms destroy

3.
plant olive trees, Deut. 28:40
olives drop off

4.
have children, Deut. 28:41
children taken captive

5.
trees and produce, Deut. 28:42
crickets destroy

The promised prosperity of YHWH is negated by the covenant disobedience of Israel!

verses.zh: 你栽种、修理葡萄园，却不得收葡萄，也不得喝葡萄酒，因为被虫子吃了。
verses.en: You will plant vineyards and cultivate them, but you will not drink wine or gather in grapes, because worms will eat them.

verses.zh: 你全境有橄榄树，却不得其油抹身，因为树上的橄榄不熟自落了。
verses.en: You will have olive trees throughout your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with olive oil, because the olives will drop off the trees while still unripe.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “your olives will drop off” (נָשַׁל, nashal), referring to the olives dropping off before they ripen. Elsewhere זַיִת (zayit, “olive”) can refer to an olive, the tree branch, the tree, or the grove. Agriculturally it might make the most sense to mean the olive flower (cf. Job 15:33). Whether the flowers drop off without being fertilized, or the olives drop off while unripe, the harvest is lost.
verses.commentary:
28:40 "anoint yourself" The people of the ANE put olive oil on their faces as a symbol of prosperity and joy
(e.g. Ruth 3:3; 2 Sam. 12:20; 14:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE

verses.zh: 你生儿养女，却不算是你的，因为必被掳去。
verses.en: You will bear sons and daughters but not keep them, because they will be taken into captivity.

verses.zh: 你所有的树木和你地里的出产必被蝗虫所吃。
verses.en: Whirring locusts[NOTE:1] will take over every tree and all the produce of your soil.
notes: The Hebrew term denotes some sort of buzzing or whirring insect; some have understood this to be a type of locust (KJV, NIV, CEV), but other insects have also been suggested: “buzzing insects” (NAB); “the cricket” (NASB); “the cicada” (NRSV).

verses.zh: 在你中间寄居的，必渐渐上升，比你高而又高；你必渐渐下降，低而又低。
verses.en: The resident foreigners[NOTE:1] who reside among you will become higher and higher over you, and you will become lower and lower.
notes: Heb “the foreigner.” This is a collective singular and has therefore been translated as plural; this includes the pronouns in the following verse, which are also singular in the Hebrew text.
verses.commentary:
28:43-44 These two verses describe the role reversal of Israelites and resident aliens (sojourners, BDB 158):

- aliens shall rise above you

- they higher and higher (BDB 751)

- you lower and lower (BDB 641) [the reversal of Deut. 28:13]

- alien shall lend to you [the reversal of Deut. 28:12]

- alien shall be the head [the reversal of Deut. 28:13]

verses.zh: 他必借给你，你却不能借给他；他必作首，你必作尾。
verses.en: They will lend to you, but you will not lend to them; they will become the head, and you will become the tail!

verses.zh: 这一切咒诅必追随你，赶上你，直到你灭亡；因为你不听从耶和华―你　神的话，不遵守他所吩咐的诫命律例。
verses.en: “All these curses will fall on you, pursuing and overtaking you until you are destroyed, because you would not obey the Lord your God by keeping his commandments and statutes that he has given[NOTE:1] you.
notes: Heb “commanded”; NAB, NIV, TEV “he gave you.”
verses.commentary:
28:45-48 Notice the cause and effect of YHWH's covenant judgments:

- the cause

- Israel would not listen (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal PERFECT) and keep (BDB 1036,
KB 1581, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUST) YHWH's commandments and statutes, Deut. 28:45; SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

- Israel did not serve (BDB 712, KB 773, Qal PERFECT [twice]) YHWH, Deut. 28:47:

(1) with joy

(2) with a glad heart

(3) thankfully for the abundance of all things

- the effect

- curses (personified)

(1) shall come on you, Deut. 28:45, BDB 97, KB 112, Qal PERFECT with waw

(2) pursue you, Deut. 28:45, BDB 922, KB 1191, Qal PERFECT with waw

(3) overtake you, Deut. 28:45, BDB 673, KB 727, Hiphil PERFECT with waw

(4) until you are destroyed, Deut. 28:45, BDB 1029, KB 1552, Niphal INFINITIVE CONSTRUST, cf. Deut. 4:25-26

- enemies

you shall serve your enemies, Deut. 28:48

(a) in hunger (BDB 944)

(b) in thirst (BDB 854)

(c) in nakedness (BDB 735)

(d) lack of all things

(e) put iron yoke on you

(f) until destroyed (BDB 1029, KB 1552, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUST, cf. Deut. 4:25-26)

verses.zh: 这些咒诅必在你和你后裔的身上成为异迹奇事，直到永远！
verses.en: These curses[NOTE:1] will be a perpetual sign and wonder with reference to you and your descendants.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “they”; the referent (the curses mentioned previously) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “seed” (so KJV, ASV).
verses.commentary: 28:46 "forever" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios).

verses.zh: 「因为你富有的时候，不欢心乐意地事奉耶和华―你的　神，
verses.en: “Because you have not served the Lord your God joyfully and wholeheartedly with the abundance of everything you have,

verses.zh: 所以你必在饥饿、干渴、赤露、缺乏之中事奉耶和华所打发来攻击你的仇敌。他必把铁轭加在你的颈项上，直到将你灭绝。
verses.en: instead in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and poverty[NOTE:1] you will serve your enemies whom the Lord will send against you. They[NOTE:2] will place an iron yoke on your neck until they have destroyed you.
notes: Heb “lack of everything.”

Heb “he” (also later in this verse). The pronoun is a collective singular referring to the enemies (cf. CEV, NLT). Many translations understand the singular pronoun to refer to the Lord (cf. NAB, NASB, NIV, NCV, NRSV, TEV).

verses.zh: 「耶和华要从远方、地极带一国的民，如鹰飞来攻击你。这民的言语，你不懂得。
verses.en: The Lord will raise up a distant nation against you, one from the other side of the earth[NOTE:1] as the eagle flies,[NOTE:2] a nation whose language you will not understand,
notes: Heb “from the end of the earth.”
Some translations understand this to mean “like an eagle swoops down” (e.g., NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT), comparing the swift attack of an eagle to the attack of the Israelites’ enemies.
verses.commentary:
28:49-57 The consequences of disobedience are continued. This paragraph lists the problems related to siege
warfare in the Ancient Near East:

- The invaded described:

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This is part of a literary unit, Deut. 27-28, which is often referred to as "the cursing and blessing" section of the Covenant.

- I think the whole OT can be seen as a consequence of Israel's inability to perform the Covenant stipulations, and thereby
was visited with the curses of Deut. 27:15-26; 28:15-68 (also note Leviticus 26).

- YHWH wanted Israel to be a revelatory channel for all the world to come to know Him. He wanted to bless Israel to gain
the attention of the nations and thereby to attract the nations unto Himself.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN.

- The curses for disobedience are more numerous than the promised blessings.

This same structure is paralleled in the treaties of the ANE.

- Meredith G. Kline, Treaty of the Great Kings: The Covenant Structure of Deuteronomy

- D. Brent Sandy and Ronald L. Giese, Jr., Cracking Old Testament Codes, pp. 125-128.

- SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (Suzerain) TREATIES

- This cursing and blessing section is parallel to Leviticus 26. This form of covenant consequences is often
called "the two ways" (cf. Deut. 30:15,19; Psalm 1).

- This is the second sermon of Moses (i.e. Deut. 5-28). The first sermon looked back to YHWH's gracious, powerful
extraction of Israel from Egypt and His presence and provision through the wilderness wandering period.

The second sermon focuses on YHWH's will for national Israel in the Promised Land. He
establishes Israel's distinctiveness so as to reveal Himself to the world.

The third sermon (Deuteronomy 29-32) deal with covenant renewal and affirmation of Israel's
loyalty and obedience to YHWH alone.

See full outline of Deuteronomy by sermons in Introduction to Deuteronomy, VIII.
